I can see the issue. In `vcardstructured_free` (line 37-45), it iterates `for (size_t i = 0; i < st->num_fields; i++)` and accesses `st->field[i]`. The `vcardstructuredtype_impl` struct has a fixed-size `field` array. Let me check the struct definition and the parameter/property code.

Now I see the key issue. The `vcardstructuredtype_impl` struct has a fixed-size `field[VCARD_MAX_STRUCTURED_FIELDS]` array (20 elements). In `vcardstructured_new_from_string` (line 59-87), the code increments `st->num_fields` without bounds checking. If the input string has more than 20 semicolon-separated fields, `st->field[st->num_fields++]` will write beyond the array bounds, corrupting memory. Then when `vcardstructured_free` iterates `for (size_t i = 0; i < st->num_fields; i++)`, it reads `st->field[i]` which may be uninitialized memory (use-of-uninitialized-value).
